events.name: Chợ Lớn Food Story 2026
events.title: Chợ Lớn Food Story 2026: Cholon Food Festival, 4–6 December
events.vn: Lễ hội Ẩm thực Chợ Lớn Food Story 2026
events.venue: An Dong Ward Public Service Centre
events.addr: 105 Trần Hưng Đạo, phường An Đông, TP.HCM
events.short: Yes, if you are in Saigon from 4 to 6 December 2026. Cholon's yearly food festival brings about 60 stalls of Vietnamese and Chinese-Vietnamese (Hoa) dishes under one roof, with cooking demos, lion and dragon dancing at the opening and music in the evenings. It is the easiest way to taste Chinatown in one evening.
why: About 60 stalls of Vietnamese and Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) dishes from Cholon's kitchens.
Opening night on Friday 4 December at 6:00 pm, with festival drums, lion dance and dragon dance.
Saturday 5 December: a hands-on session cooking signature Hoa dishes (2:00–4:00 pm) and a bicycle parade in the morning (8:00–9:00 am, planned).
Taste-and-guess games, and Vietnamese and Chinese music with acoustic sets in the evenings.
This year's theme is 'Bát Bửu – Sắc vị tinh hoa', the Eight Treasures, a nod to the lucky number 8.
events.status: The 4th edition runs 4–6 December 2026, organised by the People's Committee of An Dong Ward, Ho Chi Minh City. Stalls open from 9:00 am on 4 December, and from 7:00 am to 9:30 pm on 5 and 6 December (Thanh Nien, SGGP, October 2026). The 2025 edition drew big weekend crowds.
facts: From 9:00 am on 4 Dec (opening 6:00 pm); 7:00 am – 9:30 pm on 5–6 Dec
105 Tran Hung Dao, An Dong Ward (Cholon)
getting: Ride-hailing: ask for “105 Trần Hưng Đạo, phường An Đông”.
Bus 1 runs from the city centre towards Cholon; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026.
Combine it with Cholon's old shops: see the Cholon food guide for places nearby.
tips: Weekend evenings are the busiest; go on Friday daytime or in the mornings for shorter queues.
Bring small cash notes; not every stall takes cards.
Share dishes so you can try more stalls.
The festival is one weekend only; the rest of the year, Cholon's family shops are open daily.

tour.h: Not in town for the festival?
tour.p: A local-led street food tour covers many of the same Cholon flavours any night of the year.

events.name: Lantern Festival in Cholon (Tết Nguyên Tiêu)
events.title: Lantern Festival in Saigon's Chinatown 2027 (Tết Nguyên Tiêu, 20 Feb)
events.vn: Tết Nguyên Tiêu của người Hoa Chợ Lớn
events.kicker: Festival · 15th day of the lunar new year · Cholon
events.addr: Các hội quán và đường phố khu Chợ Lớn (phường An Đông, Chợ Lớn)
events.short: Yes: it is Cholon's biggest night of the year and a national intangible heritage. On the 15th day of the first lunar month (Saturday 20 February 2027) the Chinese community's assembly halls light up, lion and dragon troupes fill the streets and a huge parade winds through Chinatown. Expect big crowds and go early.
why: A street parade with lion, dragon and unicorn troupes, giant drums, the Eight Immortals and stilt walkers; in 2026 about 1,200 performers took part.
Cholon's old assembly halls (hội quán), such as Nghia An on Nguyen Trai street, hold rituals and lantern offerings, and some carry their deity through the neighbourhood.
An evening show at the An Dong Ward Public Service Centre, 105 Tran Hung Dao, broadcast on HTV.
The customs of the Lantern Festival of Cholon's Chinese community have been on Vietnam's national intangible heritage list since 2020.
events.status: 2027 programme not announced yet. In 2026 (3 March), An Dong Ward organised parades in the morning and late afternoon through streets such as Hai Thuong Lan Ong, Chau Van Liem, Luong Nhu Hoc and Nguyen Trai, and an evening show from 7:00 pm (Tuoi Tre, March 2026). Expect a similar shape on 20 February 2027; this page will be updated when the route is published.
facts: Cholon: assembly halls on Nguyen Trai and Tran Hung Dao, parade streets around Hai Thuong Lan Ong and Luong Nhu Hoc
getting: Ride-hailing to Nguyen Trai or Tran Hung Dao in Cholon; expect road closures along the parade route.
Walk the last stretch: streets near the parade are packed.
Bus 1 from the city centre stops in Cholon.
tips: Pick a spot along the route 30–45 minutes before the parade starts.
Keep your phone and bag close; crowds are dense.
Lion troupes 'pick' red envelopes and greens hung outside shops for luck: watch, but leave space for them.
Assembly halls are working places of worship: dress modestly and ask before photographing rituals.
events.teaser: Cholon's biggest night: the lantern-festival parade on 20 February 2027.

events.name: Lion and dragon dance in Saigon
events.title: Lion & Dragon Dance in Saigon: When and Where to See It
events.addr: Khu Chợ Lớn và các tuyến phố khắp TP.HCM
events.short: Yes, if your trip falls on the right dates. Lion (lân), lion (sư, the northern Chinese style) and dragon (rồng) troupes perform for luck at the Lunar New Year, the Lantern Festival and the Mid-Autumn Festival, and at shop openings all year. Cholon, Saigon's Chinatown, has the most troupes and the best chance of seeing one.
why: Drums, cymbals and gongs set the rhythm while two dancers inside each lion leap, bow and 'sleep'; acrobatic troupes balance on tall poles.
The lion 'plucks the greens' (lettuce and a red envelope hung over a door) to bring luck to the shop or home.
Dragons are carried on poles by a team of dancers, chasing a pearl through the street.
Some Cholon troupes also bring out the Ông Địa (Earth God) character, who fans and teases the lion.
events.status: The best fixed dates are the Lunar New Year (from Saturday 6 February 2027), the Lantern Festival parade in Cholon (Saturday 20 February 2027) and the Mid-Autumn Festival. Outside those dates you may still meet troupes at shop openings, especially in Cholon.
facts: Lunar New Year, Lantern Festival (20 Feb 2027), Mid-Autumn Festival, shop openings
Cholon streets and assembly halls; malls and hotels at Tet
Loud drums: bring ear plugs for small children
getting: Cholon is 20–30 minutes from District 1 by car; bus 1 also goes there.
At Tet, malls and big hotels in District 1 often book troupes in the first days of the year.
For the biggest show, follow the Lantern Festival parade in Cholon.
tips: Follow the drums: you will usually hear a troupe before you see it.
Don't step between the lion and the greens it is trying to reach.
Small red envelopes (lì xì) for the troupe are welcome but not expected from visitors.
events.teaser: When and where to catch lion and dragon troupes in Saigon.

events.name: Tết (Lunar New Year) in Saigon 2027
events.title: Tet 2027 in Ho Chi Minh City: Dates, What's Open & Tips (6 Feb)
events.kicker: Holiday · New Year's Day Sat 6 Feb 2027
events.q: Is it a good time to visit?
events.short: Yes, with planning. The first day of the Year of the Goat (Đinh Mùi) is Saturday 6 February 2027. The week before is festive and busy; then for the first days of the new year the city empties out, many family shops close and the streets are calm and decorated. Book transport and rooms early, and expect some places on this site to be closed.
why: The days before Tet: flower markets, kumquat and apricot-blossom trees on every motorbike, and streets hung with red lanterns.
New Year's Eve (the night of 5 February 2027): the city usually holds fireworks at several sites at midnight.
The first days of the year: quiet streets, people in new clothes visiting pagodas and family, and lion dances for luck.
Two weeks later, the Lantern Festival (20 February 2027) brings Cholon's biggest parade.
events.status: Tet 2027: New Year's Eve is Friday 5 February, the first day is Saturday 6 February. The official public-holiday schedule for 2027 had not been announced as of October 2026. Many small family shops close for several days around the first day; malls, big restaurants, hotels and tourist sights mostly stay open, sometimes with shorter hours or a holiday surcharge.
facts: The first 3 days of the new year
getting: Book flights, trains and buses out of the city weeks ahead; they sell out before Tet.
Ride-hailing still works over Tet, but expect higher prices and longer waits.
Arriving around Tet? Pre-book your airport transfer; see the airport to city guide.
tips: Check opening days before crossing town to a restaurant; many family shops close over the first days.
Say “Chúc mừng năm mới” (Happy New Year) to the people you meet.
Give and receive red envelopes (lì xì) with both hands; new, crisp notes are the custom.
Avoid sweeping, arguing or lending money on the first day; locals take first-day luck seriously.
events.teaser: Tet 2027 falls on 6 February: what's open, what closes and how to plan.
